title: On classic n-universal quadratic forms over dyadic local fields
author: Zilong He
citation: Zilong He, On classic n-universal quadratic forms over dyadic local fields, manuscripta math. 174 (2024), 559-595

authoritativeSource.description: 37-page publisher PDF; version of record published online 24 October 2023

comparisonSources.description: 33-page arXiv v3 comparison copy, revised 25 December 2025 after publication

formalizedScope: Theorem 1.1 proved equivalence for every source rank and n >= 2, with both parity branches
Classic maximality and existence of classic-maximal over-lattices
Local BONG proof chain in Sections 2-6, with source differences recorded separately
Theorem 1.5 local implication for every n >= 1 and Corollary 6.3 even branch
Section 7 ambient exhaustion and Lemma 7.4 even-rank testing equivalence
Lemma 7.10(iii) C-pair ambient exactness and integral deletion-witness core for both published parameter families
Kernel-checked refutation of the literal Lemma 7.1(ii) disjunction when e > 1
excludedScope: Theorem 1.3 full minimality, the Lemma 7.10 finite-index nonisometry bridge and exceptional-row clauses, odd-rank sufficiency, and complete published counting claims
Theorem 1.5 number-field localization and global unramifiedness/discriminant conclusion
Literal Lemma 7.1(ii) and downstream claims requiring an unresolved source correction
Global consequences and independent human semantic sign-off
reviewNotice: Theorem 1.1 has a checked proof, not merely a proposition encoding. The complete n >= 1 local-field implication underlying Theorem 1.5 is proved, including its unary branch; its number-field localization and global discriminant clause are not. Lemma 7.10(iii)'s C-pair witness mechanism is checked, but its finite-index bridge, the exceptional rows, Theorem 1.3, and the other global results remain incomplete. The false literal Lemma 7.1(ii) is disclosed and refuted, not assumed or silently repaired. Grade C describes partial coverage and is not a whole-paper certificate. The post-publication arXiv v3 copy is non-authoritative.
